unique.reason: Key point 'will protect 900 homes' drops Ruiz's hedge, caveat and the Environment Agency's uncertainty; plainly misinforms residents about flood safety.
Key points omit the January consultation, leaving the misattributed 'without consultation' claim unanswered; also omit Mill Lane access loss. Material loss of meaning.
Key point 3 turns an expected, consultation-dependent schedule into a firm one and drops 2027; real distortion of the article's plan.
innerText loses blockquote structure so speech may blur narration and quotes; real but hedged and voice-dependent.
Default voice may be a network voice sending text off-device without notice; real in some browsers, but article text is public and exposure is minor.
Mostly a pass statement plus generic process and research advice; not a distinct problem in the material.
No pause, rate or skip controls and no visible pressed style; a real but modest burden for listeners.
Browser speech can overlap a screen reader's voice and can only be stopped at the button; real minor annoyance.
Three inline links separated by middle dots inside a labelled nav is trivial noise, not worth reporting.
Known Chromium issue where long utterances stop silently; listeners could hear only the faulty key points and never reach the correction.
Fixed-label aria-pressed toggle is already the recommended pattern and 'pressed' conveys state; the stuck state is covered elsewhere.
